analysis: Interpretation, not graph proof. The proposal is a pending, un-applied revision of one open question and nothing else. Reading the two candidates side by side, the only difference is the wording of the question tied to q-conversion-settlement. The baseline asks whether the Book 20 hands-to-draw conversion is a lasting settlement or a stage the finale must revisit. The proposal asks whether the conversion reaches the shares the Mill Compact purchased, or whether those shares stay outside it, and marks that as not decided. The recorded comparison reports no added, changed or removed nodes, links, phases, emotion targets, complex emotions, genre contracts or genre interactions, and summary_changed is false. That block does not cover open-question text, so the wording change is something I read from the two candidates, not something the comparison reported. What it accomplishes: it takes the Compact-share path the author explored under h2 and turns it into an explicit open question without answering it. The record already pulls two ways. l_trade_draws_without_return and the inst_mill_compact summary say purchased draw carries no return labour. l_conversion_sets_draw and l_tally_counts_hands say that from Book 20 draw is partly set by hands owed. Nothing recorded says which rule governs a Compact-held share, so the proposal names that gap. It also sits beside q-compact-settlement, which asks what the Compact will give for settling its claim; the two now share the Compact's relationship to hands, though neither is answered. Kept: every other question and its id, the open_question_ids list, all nodes, links, phases, emotion targets and genre contracts, and the Compact's grain-labour question. Transformed: the conversion question changes from a question about time (does it last) into a question about scope (whom it binds). That scope question is the one that decides whether the pastoral engine, belonging produced by return labour and eroded by unshared draw, reaches the Compact at all, and it bears on the et_cost_of_counting thread. Displaced: the earlier concern that the conversion might be a stage the finale must revisit is no longer asked anywhere in the proposed list. It is not wholly lost, since q-finale-mechanism still asks which finale mechanism governs who gives labour and who is counted, and Alternatives A and B already treat the conversion differently (A decouples draw from hands, B owes hands by draw). But no question now asks the author to decide the conversion's durability as such. Whether that is a deliberate trade or a loss is for the author to say.

uncertainties: author_decision: the review context shows the author asked for a wording-only change to this one question, with every other element left as it is and the answer not decided. I take that as given and have not judged whether it should be applied.

The comparison block lists no changed components and does not cover open-question text. I found the wording difference by reading both candidates, so a consumer relying only on the comparison block would see no change.

speculative_possibility: if the author later answers that the conversion binds Compact shares, the Compact's grain-labour question (q-compact-settlement) and Alternative B's l_compact_hands_in_kind would need creative development to say whether grain-labour counts as hands. If the answer is that the Compact is exempt, the household's decline would sit against an untouched neighbour, which also needs development. Neither is recorded.

speculative_possibility: dropping the durability wording could leave the question of whether the Book 20 conversion lasts unasked unless q-finale-mechanism is read to cover it. Whether that matters depends on how the author wants the finale to treat the conversion.

The reworded question uses the Compact-share path from the h2 alternative as its origin, but h2 asserted the conversion applies to every share, while the proposal only asks. The proposal carries h2's subject, not its answer, and the record does not show whether the author prefers the h2 reading.

Which earlier concerns count as kept, transformed or displaced is my interpretation of the question texts. The record does not state how the author ranks the durability concern against the scope concern.
